events.name: The Offer
events.intro: N, speaking fast, not quite looking at you: "Your Pokémon just said something. Did you hear? No. Nobody does. It said it wasn't afraid of you. That's rare. I've listened to four hundred. Eleven said that." N: "I can't go back in. They'd kneel. I'd say "get up" and they'd take it for a blessing. But I need to know what they're for, now. What he's made of them. Would you go? You'd be my ears. It's the only part of me that was ever any use." N: "If you come out thinking I was wrong to leave, I'll listen. I always listen."

events.name: A Dog at a Fence
events.intro: A hillside with a castle coming out of it. Scaffolding. Wet stone. Six hundred people in white, with candles, digging by hand. A Knight, at the gate, holding out an open hand, flat and low: "Welcome, Listener. That's what you're called till you've heard something. It's not a rank. It's a state." A Chandelure overhead, burning steadily: the Vigil's Votive. It's never gone out. Somebody's always awake to see it doesn't. The oath is one line, and you say it: "I'll not hold what hasn't chosen me." The Knight: "You'll be asked to prove it. Not today. We don't ask it of Listeners. But you'll see it done, at dusk, and you'll know what you're walking toward."

success.text: A vaulted room. Two hundred pallets. A window at ground level that looks out at boots.

events.name: The Lower Dormitory
events.intro: Yara Fairchild, twenty, folding a tabard with great care: "You're beside me. I'm Yara. I'm a Knight; I did mine in spring." Yara: "A Lillipup. I'd had her from an egg. He said: "Did she choose you, or were you just there first?" And I couldn't say. So I knelt." Yara: "It was the right thing. He said. She's free now. I go on Sundays. She comes to the fence. She thinks I'm coming back for her." She's very steady about it. Yara: "She's free. That's what free looks like. It looks like a dog at a fence."

success.text: Yara: "That's not the question. The question's whether she's better. I'm not supposed to count."
Yara: "The king could've. He's away. They say when he's back he'll walk every field and tell us what they said." A pause. Yara: "I think about what she'll have said."
She folds the tabard again. It was already folded. Yara: "Then I'd be someone who took it back. I'd have done it for nothing. Don't say that to me again, please."

events.name: The Release
events.intro: Dusk. You watch from the fence line. A boy of sixteen, a Tepig. Sage Gorm, sonorous: "It was never yours." The boy: "I'll not hold what hasn't chosen me." He stands. He turns. He walks. He doesn't look back; that's the rule. The Tepig trots after him. It gets to the fence. It puts its nose through. You're the only one facing that way.

success.text: The Tepig sits. It watches the boy to the top of the hill.
That's what a Knight does.

choices.label: (Hold out an open hand. Flat. Low.)

success.text: The old gesture. The Tepig looks at it. It comes over. It sniffs. It looks back at the hill. It stays with you till the candle's lit. Sister Ianthe, behind: "Where did you learn that? That's the old way. That's what it was for."

events.name: The Lower Dormitory
events.intro: Night. A lamp at the far end. An old woman in the old white, mending. Sister Ianthe Moncrieff: "I tend the king's room. It's being dug out; they've found the door. I was his nurse. I'm told that's an honour. I'll tell you what it was, when I know you." End of Act 1: a white hood. A candle. A collecting tin, with your name on it.

success.text: It's warm from the last person. Somebody's always awake.

events.name: The Wrong House
events.intro: A lane in Striaton. Washing on a line. A white-hooded man of forty checking an address against a paper, twice. Emil Hawksmoor: "You're the Listener. Emil. I was nineteen years an orderly at a Center. D'you know what an orderly does? He patches them up and hands them back. To the same people. "He fell." "She's clumsy." I've handed back a Herdier three times to a man who called it clumsy." Emil: "I'm done handing them back. So. A visit. The order says: neglected Pansage. Number nine."

success.text: A front garden. A gate with a child's wellingtons beside it.

events.name: Number Nine
events.intro: On the windowsill, in the sun: a Pansage. Fat. Asleep. It's got a ribbon on. Taped to the glass above it: a drawing, in crayon, of a green thing with a ribbon on. BEST FREND. Emil: "...This isn't the house. It can't be. Check the address." It's the address. Yara: "It could be— appearances. He says we can't tell from outside." Emil: "I've nineteen years of telling from outside. That's a Pokémon that's never missed a meal or been shouted at. Look at its ears." You have the order. "Liberation Order 114. Pansage, juvenile, unusual colouring. PRIORITY. — Z."

success.text: A child's face at the window. The screen cuts to the lane, and Emil standing in it with a carrier, not moving. Emil doesn't speak for the rest of the stage.

choices.label: "Leave it. Tell them the house was empty."

success.text: "The house was empty." Emil, to the windowsill: "Stay fat."

Emil: ""Z." Zinzolin." He takes a folded bundle from inside his tabard. He's been keeping them. Emil: "That's the fourth this month. A Vanillite with a gold sheen. An Axew, "unusually large." An Eevee." A pause. Emil: "None of them said "neglected." I read "neglected." I read it because it's what I came here to read." It's the first thread.

events.name: Number Nine
events.intro: The Pansage sleeps on. The order's still in your hand.

success.text: A child's face at the window. The screen cuts to the lane, and Emil standing in it with a carrier, not moving. Emil doesn't speak for the rest of the stage.

events.name: The Van
events.intro: As you leave: a black van at the end of the lane. Two of the Crew, leaning on it. A Crew Grunt, to the white hoods, amused: "All right, candles? Got it?" Emil: "Who are you?" The Crew Grunt: "Collections. You lot do the crying, we do the lifting. It's a system." He looks at your empty hands. The Crew Grunt: "No? Never mind. We'll come back when you've gone. We've a key." Yara: "A key to what?"

success.text: Two of the Crew, and they don't expect a white hood to stand anywhere.
The Crew Grunt: "Commander Aldith's. Who's yours? A candle?" He laughs. He gets back in the van. It doesn't leave.
Behind you, the van door slides. Emil doesn't look back. It's the rule.

remembers.notice: Commander Aldith, by radio, after: "Who was that? White hoods? Fighting us? Put it in the report as weather."

events.name: A Red Collar
events.intro: The Dreamyard. A ruined factory. A sign, new: RESETTLEMENT. NO ADMITTANCE TO KNIGHTS. Pink mist at ankle height. A Munna, watching. Yara: ""Resettlement." That's where they go after the fields. It's a good word. It means there's a place." Emil: "It means there's a sign."

success.text: Past the sign.

events.name: The Floor
events.intro: Not a field. Not a forest. Crates. Stacked four high, in rows, with air holes. A stencil on each: a type, a level, a number. A Sage at a desk with a ledger. He's got a thick neck and a candle he hasn't lit. Sage Giallo, not looking up: "Knights aren't permitted. It says so on the sign. I had the sign made." Yara: "That's— those are ours. The ones we freed. That's a Lillipup. That's—" She's stopped. Yara: "That's a Lillipup with a red collar." It's seen her. Its whole back end's going. It's been in a crate since Monday, and its person's come, as it always knew she would. Nothing's hurt here, and nothing has been. They're fed. They're kept. They're being held for one man's army.

success.text: It's on the desk. Giallo's stood up.

events.name: The Ledger
events.intro: Columns. Date. Field. Species. "Released by." "Collected." "Assigned." Under "Assigned," in every row, the same word: Hold. The Frigate's hold.

success.text: Emil's beside you. It's the first time he's ever sent a Pokémon at a person.

Emil knocks over the candle. Giallo turns. Yara's got the crate open and shut in the time it takes. She carries it under her tunic for the rest of the region. It doesn't make a sound. It's good at this. It's been waiting quietly since spring.
Nothing's opened. You walk out. Act 4 comes early, and angrier. Yara looks back the whole way. It's the rule that she mustn't. She does.

events.name: Room Four
events.intro: Sage Giallo: "I guard. It's all I've ever done. Step away from the crates."

success.text: Sage Giallo doesn't light the candle.

remembers.notice: Yara's gone with the Lillipup before it ends. Win, and sixty Pokémon go into the Dreamyard, and the Munna's mist comes up to cover them going.

events.name: The Mist
events.intro: In the mist, going out, the Munna shows you one thing: a tall man with a cane, standing over a crate, saying nothing. It's what it shows everyone here. It's the only thing it's seen for a year. You take the ledger: the Dreamyard Ledger. Sixty rows. Sixty towns.

success.text: The sign says NO ADMITTANCE TO KNIGHTS on the way out, too.

events.name: Not Admitted
events.intro: A half-dug doorway. A child's room, untouched. A toy train going round. A basketball hoop, too low now. A music box. N, on the floor, knees up, watching the train: "You came. I flew in under the cloud; nobody saw. I shouldn't be here. If they find me they'll put a crown on me, and I'll have to be polite about it." N: "This is where I grew up. He brought them here. The ones people had hurt. A Darumaka with a burn. A Zorua that wouldn't let anyone touch its tail. I thought that's what people did. I was eleven before I met a Pokémon that was happy. I thought it was lying." N: "I've done the sum. If every trainer's like the ones who hurt my friends, I'm right. If they aren't— how many would it take? To make me wrong? I keep meeting ones that aren't afraid. I've a list. You're on it. Your team is on it." N: "Tell me about the Dreamyard. Don't make it kind."

success.text: The train goes round three times while you talk. He doesn't interrupt. At "Hold," he puts his hand flat on the floor, as if something had moved under it. Sister Ianthe's in the doorway. events.name: The Seventh Chair
events.intro: The Hall of Sages. Seven chairs. Six with dust. A man with a cane, standing behind the seventh, with a cloth in his hand. Ghetsis: "Ah. The Listener. You've seen the Dreamyard. Good. I dislike explaining." Ghetsis: "Sit. No, not that one. This one. I dusted it myself. Do you know how long it's been since I did a thing with my own hands that wasn't a lie?" Ghetsis: "The boy was a key I cut myself. Fourteen years. He opened every door in Unova and then walked out of the last one, which I hadn't foreseen: I'd made him to listen, and he did. You're cleverer than he is. You've seen the crates and you're still in the hood. Tomorrow a king's crowned on that balcony. Stand beside the throne and look moved."

success.text: You stay standing. Ghetsis: "A Sage who stands. How original." He goes. In the corner, three shapes that were there the whole time. One of the Shadow Triad: "He gave us names. Then he took them back." Another: "The King gave things names. A train. A ball." The third: "Ask him for three more. We'd take any."

Ghetsis: "What it needs. That he's coming back. They've dug out a castle with their hands on the strength of it. I find that affecting. I mean that. I'm affected by it the way one's affected by a very good lock."

events.name: The Night Before
events.intro: The lower dormitory. The night before. Six hundred candles. The Votive overhead. The word's gone round. A Knight, shining: "He's back. They've seen him. He's in the king's room; the Sister's seen a light." Another: "He'll walk the fields. He'll tell us what they said." Yara's on her pallet, on her side, facing the wall, with one arm under her tunic. Something under there sighs. Yara, very low: "I've a dog in my shirt and a king coming in the morning to tell me I was right to let her go. I don't know which of those I'm going to have to give up." Emil, on the next pallet, on his back, hands locked on his chest: "If he's lied to that boy the way they lied to me at the Center, I'll— I don't know what I'll do. I'm a nurse. I've only ever been angry at things." Your last choice of the night: who's told about the balcony.

success.text: The Vigil kneels in the morning, whole.
They know. In every ending, they act on it.

You stand under the Votive and say it. Nobody believes it. Not one. These people aren't tired. They've faith. A Knight: "You've been listening to the black coats." You're found out, and put out of the gate. You're on the hill in the morning, with N, looking in.

remembers.notice: In the corner, the three shapes are still there. One of them says, to nobody: "Ask him for three more."

events.name: Zinzolin, Alone
events.intro: A cold room. He's in furs. Zinzolin: "I feel the cold more than other men. It's the only thing I feel. Ghetsis keeps me close because I've no warmth to betray him with."

success.text: Zinzolin: "Mine. In my hand. His words. "Priority." I've never once wanted a gold Vanillite. I'm cold enough."
He does, a little. He holds his hands out to it as if it were a thing he'd read about.
Zinzolin: "To be cold with company." He names the Dreamyard's other sites, one by one, as if they were rooms in a house he'd lived in.

events.name: Colress, Alone
events.intro: A lab. He's delighted to see anyone. Colress: "I don't care about liberation! I care what brings out a Pokémon's strength. Ghetsis says force. The King says freedom. I say: test it. You're a splendid data point. Yours fight harder than either theory predicts."

success.text: Colress: "Is it! Can you show me? Under controlled conditions?"
Colress: "Then it's the best kind! An inconvenient answer is one nobody's paid for yet."
Colress: "A man with a cane. I don't ask what he funds next door. That's a lie. I ask. He answers beautifully."

events.name: Controlled Conditions
events.intro: A sparring match, under controlled conditions. He's got a clipboard and a grin.

success.text: Colress: "Splendid! Again! No, don't hold back for the data's sake."

events.name: The Shadow Triad
events.intro: They're simply there. One of them: "He found us. He named us. He took the names back when we were useful. Ask the King to give us one. We'd take any."

success.text: You pick three. They don't thank you. They say them over, once each, under their breath. They're gone from Ghetsis's side in the throne room.
The second: "We don't ask. We were made not to." The third: "...We'll think about it."
A long pause. The first: "We don't remember. That was the point of taking them."

remembers.notice: You've the harbourmaster's entry, copied out.

success.text: You read them out. One of the Triad: "...Wick." Another: "That's—" The third, who was always cold: "Tallow. I was— there was soup." They don't thank you. They're gone. In every ending, they aren't at his shoulder.
